hero.headline: DHS finds detainees held in metal enclosures at Alligator Alcatraz; DeSantis defends facility
hero.body:
A Department of Homeland Security inspector general report found serious health and safety failures at Florida's now-closed Everglades immigration detention center, including the use of small metal enclosures to hold detainees for nearly two hours. The findings emerged amid an unresolved fight over the $250 million in emergency spending lawmakers approved and more than $417 million in unpaid invoices tied to the state's broader immigration operations.

The federal review followed an unannounced January inspection. Records showed that 79 detainees had been confined in metal enclosures offering about 18 square feet of floor space between July 17, 2025, and January. Stays ranged from several minutes to nearly two hours, with detainees exposed to outdoor temperatures. Inspectors described the practice as unprecedented among detention facilities their office had inspected and a significant risk to detainees' health and safety. Staff described the spaces as calming areas for people seeking time alone. Inspectors also identified an instance in which an enclosure was used after a detainee failed to follow a command.

Gov. Ron DeSantis defended the operation Monday, saying it helped federal authorities deport people who otherwise could have returned to Florida communities. Speaking in Lakeland, DeSantis acknowledged he had not reviewed the findings. He estimated that Florida's detention assistance helped federal authorities detain and deport about 25,000 people, referring to both Alligator Alcatraz and a Baker County operation. DeSantis also said the federal government had approved reimbursement for the state's work.

The review documented insects in bathing areas, showers limited to three times a week and inadequate recreation. Inspectors also found shortcomings in medical care and food service. Staff could not consistently identify which detention standards applied, according to the report. The inspector general administratively closed all 10 recommendations because the facility had ceased operating in June.

The controversy also became a fight over the governor's authority. The Republican-controlled Legislature adopted Senate Bill 7040, which requires quarterly emergency-fund reports covering cash flow, reimbursements, assets and unpaid invoices. The law also subjects spending after emergency renewals to legislative budget review procedures.

FDEM submitted its overdue spending report Friday, Sept. 11, shortly before lawmakers approved another $250 million for emergency expenses, including immigration costs, according to reporting by The Florida Trib published by WLRN. That report showed Florida had received $84.5 million of an expected $608 million in federal reimbursement for detention centers. It also listed more than $417 million in unpaid immigration-related invoices as of June 30. Those figures cover the broader immigration effort, rather than a final accounting of Alligator Alcatraz alone.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce pair who fired guns while drinking face only misdemeanor charges
hero.body:
Two Fort Pierce residents accused of firing multiple guns while drinking in a residential neighborhood face only misdemeanor charges under Florida law, even as a neighbor described bullets flying near his home with his 5-year-old son present.

Tiffany Rose Lindo and Jacob Robert Mills, both 25, were arrested after St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputies responded around 9 p.m. Saturday to the 5100 block of Happiness Street following reports of people actively firing guns. Investigators say the pair fired a shotgun, rifle and handguns into the ground and had consumed alcohol before and during the incident. Each faces charges of discharging a firearm in a public or residential area and using a firearm while under the influence of alcohol.

Both charges are misdemeanors under Florida law based on the allegations announced by the Sheriff's Office. The firearm-discharge offense is a first-degree misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail, while using a firearm while impaired by alcohol is a second-degree misdemeanor that can carry up to 60 days in jail. Fort Pierce criminal defense attorney Brian Mallonee said the specific circumstances surrounding where and how a gun is fired determine the charge level. More serious allegations could potentially lead to different charges if a bullet struck a home, vehicle or person, Mallonee said, but prosecutors would still have to prove the elements of the charges.

The neighbor who called 911 told CBS12 News he feared someone was being shot when he heard what he described as a barrage of gunfire Saturday night. He said he heard two gunshots, then a barrage of AR-15 rounds, then shotgun blasts, and then another barrage of AR-15 rounds roughly 300 feet away. The neighbor, who asked that his face not be shown, said his 5-year-old son stays with him every other week. Wood and drywall don't stop bullets, he said. The bullets could've came through the wall and hit my son. No one was injured in the incident. Lindo and Mills have both bonded out of jail, and the Sheriff's Office said the firearms involved were taken as evidence but the pair will have an opportunity to get the guns back once the case is resolved.

It kind of freaked me out a little bit, just not knowing what direction or where they were shooting, he said. Wood and drywall don't stop bullets. The concern was especially personal. The neighbor said his 5-year-old son stays with him every other week. The bullets could've came through the wall and hit my son, he said. Why are the charges misdemeanors? Despite the potential danger described by the neighbor, both charges are misdemeanors under Florida law based on the allegations announced by the Sheriff's Office. CBS12 News asked Fort Pierce criminal defense attorney Brian Mallonee why the alleged conduct does not automatically result in a felony. You'd have to ask your lawmakers that, Mallonee said. That would be a question for the guys in Tallahassee. Mallonee explained that Florida's firearm-discharge law includes specific circumstances surrounding where and how a gun is fired. The size of a property and density of the surrounding residential area can matter, but he said negligently or recklessly firing a weapon can be illegal regardless of property size. The firearm-discharge offense can be a first-degree misdemeanor, punishable by up to one year in county jail. Mallonee said any eventual sentence would depend on factors including a defendant's prior record and how reckless or negligent the conduct was. Florida also separately prohibits using a firearm while impaired by alcohol or certain controlled substances. That offense is a second-degree misdemeanor, which can carry up to 60 days in jail. Mallonee said allegations involving alcohol could also factor into questions about whether someone's handling or discharge of a firearm was negligent or reckless. hero.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after second bomb threat this month
hero.body:
Students and staff at Martin County High School were evacuated Monday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted a response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The incident marks the second bomb threat reported at the school this month, raising concerns among parents and school staff as authorities continue investigating.

In a message sent to families, school officials said all buildings were being evacuated at the direction of law enforcement while authorities investigate the threat. "We are currently evacuating all buildings under the direction of the Martin County Sheriff's Office due to a bomb threat. The safety of our students and staff remains our highest priority," school officials said.

No injuries have been reported.

School leaders thanked families for their patience and cooperation during the evacuation and emphasized that student and staff safety remains the top priority. The school said it is working closely with law enforcement and will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is expected to provide further information as the investigation continues.

cards.headline: Old Havana Cafe, House of Hope set world record with 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City
cards.teaser: Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich Saturday morning in Palm City, breaking the previous world record held by Tampa and raising more than $30,000 for local programs.
cards.body:
Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich Saturday morning in Palm City, breaking the previous world record held by Tampa. The event raised more than $30,000 for House of Hope, a Martin County nonprofit that provides food assistance, job training, education and other services aimed at helping local families become more self-sufficient.

A large crowd turned out to watch volunteers and sandwich builders assemble the record-breaking Cuban sandwich and support the fundraiser. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi was on hand to complete the final measurement confirming the sandwich reached 400 feet.

Organizers said the event was about more than setting a world record. The event was designed to bring the community together while raising awareness and support for House of Hope's mission.

Martin County is now home to the world's longest Cuban sandwich.

hero.headline: Four bomb threats hit Treasure Coast in eight days; police probe Russia link
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police and the FBI are investigating four bomb threats reported across the Treasure Coast over the last eight days, including a Saturday threat that evacuated visitor areas at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Three of the four threats were sent by email, and investigators are working to determine whether the incidents are connected.

Police cruisers surrounded Lawnwood Hospital Saturday afternoon as officers searched the building after receiving an emailed threat. Visitor areas were evacuated as a precaution, and police gave the all-clear several hours later. Patient care was not interrupted. Police said the threat followed similar patterns to a threat reported Friday at Indian River State College and threats made at two Treasure Coast area high schools.

The first threat was called in at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday, September 4. Students were evacuated while deputies investigated. Investigators said the email address used to send the threat to Martin County High School had been hacked and may have been connected to a suspect in Russia. None of the threats were found to be credible, but officers continue to take each one seriously. No explosives were found in any of the incidents.

Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department said investigators will continue working to identify whoever is behind the threats. "Once we narrow this down, those who are making these threats, we will find you and we will prosecute you," Santiago said. Dan Toback, who lives in Port St. Lucie and runs a community news page called SLC Scanner, said the threats are creating unnecessary fear in the community. "These threats that are coming out are people that are simply trying to cause fear, nothing more," Toback said. All four incidents remain under investigation. Police are asking anyone with information about the threats to contact investigators.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after eight explosive devices found at Balsam Drive home
hero.body:
Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after investigators found eight improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials at his home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday.

Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of a risk protection order.

At approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday, detectives with the SLCSO Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence when they identified suspected destructive devices, Fort Pierce police said in a news release Friday morning. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team.

Bomb technicians responded to the residence and conducted a preliminary examination of the suspected devices. Technicians removed seven devices from the residence and safely secured them in a containment vessel. Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," Sheriff Richard Del Toro said. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices. I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation."

The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no immediate threat to the community.

Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

hero.headline: Fourth bomb threat in two weeks targets Lawnwood Hospital; FBI joins probe
hero.body:
A bomb threat emailed to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital on Saturday marked the fourth such threat made via email in less than two weeks on the Treasure Coast. Fort Pierce police are now working with the FBI to track down the source.

Police learned an email was sent just before 11 a.m. Saturday alleging two bombs were planted inside the hospital. The Fort Pierce Police Department mobilized and partially evacuated the facility. A spokesperson for HCA said patient care was not impacted, and visitors were asked to wait outside while police swept the two areas mentioned in the threat. Authorities ultimately determined the threat was not credible.

Fort Pierce police said Saturday's threat was similar in nature to a threat made at nearby Indian River State College earlier this week, as well as two threats at Treasure Coast area high schools. Law enforcement responded to Fort Pierce Central High School last week. Parent Angela Jones described her reaction when she learned there was a threat. "I was concerned. I was like, what's going on? I got a phone call from the school stating that it was a bomb threat," Jones said. On Thursday, a similar situation unfolded at Martin County High School. Nothing was found at any of the campuses. Police said all of the recent incidents are being investigated holistically.

Former State Attorney for Palm Beach County Dave Aronberg said law enforcement is getting better at tracking down suspects in these cases, even when jurisdictional issues arise depending on where a threat originated. "They have a lot of advanced tools who can, that can track people and find out through IP addresses and other means. They can issue subpoenas," Aronberg said. Aronberg also outlined the serious legal consequences for anyone found responsible. "Florida law makes it a 2nd-degree felony to compose and send any written or electronic record that includes emails or text messages that threaten to kill or do bodily injury or conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism. So you're talking about a serious felony punishment of up to 15 years in prison," Aronberg said.

hero.headline: Fourth bomb threat in under two weeks forces partial evacuation at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital
hero.body:
A bomb threat emailed to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital on Saturday forced a partial evacuation of the facility and marked the fourth such threat made via email in less than two weeks on the Treasure Coast. Fort Pierce police are now working with the FBI to track down the source.

Police learned an email was sent just before 11 a.m. Saturday alleging two bombs were planted inside the hospital. The Fort Pierce Police Department mobilized and partially evacuated the facility. A spokesperson for HCA said patient care was not impacted, and visitors were asked to wait outside while police swept the two areas mentioned in the threat. Authorities ultimately determined the threat was not credible.

Fort Pierce police said Saturday's threat was similar in nature to a threat made at nearby Indian River State College earlier this week, as well as two threats at Treasure Coast area high schools. Fort Pierce Central High School received a threat last week, followed by a similar situation at Martin County High School on Thursday. Nothing was found at any of the campuses. Police said all of the recent incidents are being investigated holistically.

Former State Attorney for Palm Beach County Dave Aronberg said law enforcement is getting better at tracking down suspects in these cases, even when jurisdictional issues arise depending on where a threat originated. "They have a lot of advanced tools who can, that can track people and find out through IP addresses and other means. They can issue subpoenas," Aronberg said. Aronberg also outlined the serious legal consequences for anyone found responsible. "Florida law makes it a 2nd-degree felony to compose and send any written or electronic record that includes emails or text messages that threaten to kill or do bodily injury or conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism. So you're talking about a serious felony punishment of up to 15 years in prison," Aronberg said.

Angela Jones, a parent at Fort Pierce Central High School, described her reaction when she learned there was a threat. "I was concerned. I was like, what's going on? I got a phone call from the school stating that it was a bomb threat," Jones said.

cards.headline: Two Fort Pierce residents arrested after firing weapons at Happiness Street residence

cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested two Fort Pierce residents after responding to reports of people actively discharging firearms at a residence in the 5100 block of Happiness Street on Sept. 12.

Deputies responded at approximately 9 p.m. following reports of gunfire. A witness reported seeing a man and a woman firing multiple weapons, including a shotgun, rifle and handguns. Deputies determined the subjects were firing the weapons into the ground. Investigators learned both subjects had been consuming alcohol before and during the incident.

Tiffany Rose Lindo, 25, and Jacob Roibert Mills, 25, both of Fort Pierce, were each arrested and charged with discharging a firearm in a public or residential area and use of a firearm while under the influence of alcohol. No one was injured.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie honors 25th anniversary of 9/11 with remembrance ceremony
cards.teaser: Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered Friday morning at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center memorial to mark 25 years since the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie held its annual 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony Friday morning at the Memorial Fountain at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center, marking the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered to honor the victims and survivors of the 2001 tragedy.

Mayor Shannon Martin, Police Chief Leo Niemczyk, St. Lucie County Fire District Firefighter/Paramedic Allen Civita and other local public safety leaders took part in the ceremony. Retired New York City Police Department detective Rafael Diaz served as the guest speaker, and the Port St. Lucie High School Choir performed.

Port St. Lucie resident Michael Cozzolino said the anniversary brought back memories of watching the attacks unfold while he was in Florida for work. "I remember I was living in Connecticut at the time, I was here in Florida, had no way back, just a rental car, and we all piled in a rental car and drove back," Cozzolino said. "I'll never forget that day." Cozzolino said the uncertainty in the hours after the attacks was frightening. "Especially being a defense contractor. Don't know where they're going to hit next," he said.

Cozzolino, a member of the Nam Knights Motorcycle Club of America, said the anniversary remains especially emotional for many first responders and veterans. "We have 84 chapters in the United States. We have 16 here, 17 here alone in Florida. About 1,400 members," Cozzolino said. "A lot of them were from New York. So, a lot of first responders, and a lot of them have the cancer now." Cozzolino said seeing the community gather at the memorial was meaningful. "The way they do this, they have the steel flowers, flags. Very patriotic here," Cozzolino said. "This town's very diverse town, and it's a great town to live in." The Port St. Lucie ceremony was one of several events across the region marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks.

hero.headline: Palm City sets world record with 400-foot Cuban sandwich to fight food insecurity
hero.body:
Community members in Palm City built a 400-foot Cuban sandwich at Justin Wilson Memorial Park on Sandpiper Way, setting a world record and raising funds for House of Hope, a nonprofit that serves more than 30,000 Martin County residents facing hunger each month.

The previous record was 365 feet, set in Tampa in 2024. The event, called Bite Into History: The Longest Cuban Sandwich Ever Made, was a joint effort of Old Havana Cafe at 2225 SE Ocean Blvd. and House of Hope. Organizers said the event was intended to call attention to food insecurity, foster community spirit and celebrate Hispanic heritage. Members of the public could purchase sandwiches.

The Doris M. Carter Family Foundation, the event's presenting sponsor, pledged to match every donation made through the event up to $15,000, doubling every donor's impact in the community.

Founded in 1984, House of Hope empowers Martin County residents to overcome hunger and hardship. The organization helps with basic needs such as food, clothing, furniture and financial assistance, as well as longer-term case management services. House of Hope has service centers in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Jensen Beach, with thrift stores in Stuart, Hobe Sound and Indiantown. The organization also operates the Growing Hope Farm in Palm City and several nutrition gardens that provide sustainable sources of fresh produce for clients as well as nutrition education and vocational opportunities to the community.

A Cuban sandwich is ham, roasted pork, Swiss cheese, pickles, mustard and sometimes salami on Cuban bread. Tampa and Miami have a rivalry over which city claims the sandwich as its own. In 2012, the Tampa City Council named it the city's official signature sandwich. Around the 1900s, cafes in Ybor City and nearby West Tampa sold the sandwiches to immigrant workers who were part of the cigar factories. By the 1960s, Cuban sandwiches were common in Miami with a large influx of Cuban residents after Fidel Castro's 1959 rise to power in their native land.

hero.headline: Fourth bomb threat in under two weeks prompts Lawnwood Hospital evacuation
hero.body:
A bomb threat emailed to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital Saturday marked the fourth such threat made via email in less than two weeks on the Treasure Coast. Fort Pierce police are now working with the FBI to track down the source.

Police learned an email was sent just before 11 a.m. Saturday alleging two bombs were planted inside the hospital. The Fort Pierce Police Department mobilized and partially evacuated the facility. A hospital spokesperson said patient care was not impacted, and visitors were asked to wait outside while police swept the two areas mentioned in the threat. Authorities ultimately determined the threat was not credible.

Fort Pierce police said Saturday's threat was similar in nature to a threat made at Indian River State College earlier this week, as well as two threats at Treasure Coast area high schools. Fort Pierce Central High School received a threat last week. Parent Angela Jones described her reaction when she learned there was a threat. "I was concerned. I was like, what's going on? I got a phone call from the school stating that it was a bomb threat," Jones said. On Thursday, a similar situation unfolded at Martin County High School. Nothing was found at any of the campuses. Police said all of the recent incidents are being investigated holistically.

Former State Attorney for Palm Beach County Dave Aronberg said law enforcement is getting better at tracking down suspects in these cases, even when jurisdictional issues arise depending on where a threat originated. "They have a lot of advanced tools who can, that can track people and find out through IP addresses and other means. They can issue subpoenas," Aronberg said. Aronberg also outlined the serious legal consequences for anyone found responsible. "Florida law makes it a 2nd-degree felony to compose and send any written or electronic record that includes emails or text messages that threaten to kill or do bodily injury or conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism. So you're talking about a serious felony punishment of up to 15 years in prison," Aronberg said.

cards.headline: Man arrested after bomb squad removes 8 improvised explosives from Fort Pierce home
cards.teaser: Detectives serving a risk protection order at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive discovered suspected destructive devices, prompting a bomb squad response and the removal of eight improvised explosive devices.
cards.body:
Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after detectives discovered improvised explosive devices at his residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested Morrone following an investigation that began Thursday. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

At approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday, detectives with the SLCSO Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence when they identified suspected destructive devices, Fort Pierce police said in a news release Friday morning. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team.

Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination of the suspected devices and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel. Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. This brought the total number of improvised explosive devices recovered from the residence to eight.

Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of a risk protection order. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action. The investigation remains ongoing.

Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, told WPBF's Ari Hait he was surprised to see such activity near his home. Rates described the area as peaceful. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

cards.headline: Two Fort Pierce residents arrested for firing weapons into ground while intoxicated
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies arrested two people after they fired multiple weapons into the ground while drinking alcohol on Happiness Street in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested two Fort Pierce residents after responding to reports of people actively discharging firearms at a residence on Happiness Street on Sept.

Deputies responded at approximately 9 p.m. to the 5100 block of Happiness Street following the reports. A witness reported seeing a man and a woman firing multiple weapons, including a shotgun, rifle and handguns.

Deputies determined the subjects were firing the weapons into the ground. Investigators learned both subjects had been consuming alcohol before and during the incident. The individuals were identified as Tiffany Rose Lindo, 25, and Jacob Roibert Mills, 25, both of Fort Pierce. Lindo and Mills were each charged with discharging a firearm in a public or residential area and use of a firearm while under the influence of alcohol. No one was injured.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police clear HCA Lawnwood Hospital after bomb threat
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department investigated a bomb threat at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital on Saturday afternoon and found no suspicious items or devices.

Police said just after 2 p.m. on September 12 they began investigating the threat. Officers arrived at the hospital and conducted an extensive search of the buildings. The Police Department announced at 3:36 p.m. that no suspicious items or devices were found.

A hospital spokesperson confirmed there was a temporary evacuation of visitors. Patient care was never impacted, the spokesperson said.

cards.headline: Eight suspected explosive devices seized from Fort Pierce home; man arrested
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a 57-year-old Fort Pierce man and seized eight suspected improvised explosive devices, bomb-making materials, and eight firearms from a home on Balsam Drive.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, and seized eight suspected improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials from his home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive following an investigation that began Thursday. Morrone faces eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Detectives with the SLCSO Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence at approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday when they identified suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel.

Detectives obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the search, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed, bringing the total to eight devices. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of the risk protection order. The FBI and ATF are assisting with the investigation.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices," Del Toro said. "I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation." The investigation remains ongoing. The sheriff's office said there is no immediate threat to the community.

Neighbors expressed concern about the situation. Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," Rates said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 9/11 ceremony draws first responders, residents 25 years later
cards.teaser: Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered Friday morning at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center to honor victims and survivors of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks on the 25th anniversary of the tragedy.
cards.body:
Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered Friday morning at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center in Port St. Lucie to honor victims and survivors of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks on the 25th anniversary of the tragedy. The city's annual 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony was held at the Memorial Fountain at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center.

Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin, Police Chief Leo Niemczyk, St. Lucie County Fire District Firefighter/Paramedic Allen Civita and other local public safety leaders took part in the ceremony. Retired New York City Police Department detective Rafael Diaz served as guest speaker, and the Port St. Lucie High School Choir performed.

Port St. Lucie resident Michael Cozzolino said the anniversary brought back memories of watching the attacks unfold while he was in Florida for work. "I remember I was living in Connecticut at the time, I was here in Florida, had no way back, just a rental car, and we all piled in a rental car and drove back," Cozzolino said. "I'll never forget that day." Cozzolino said the uncertainty in the hours after the attacks was frightening. "Especially being a defense contractor. Don't know where they're going to hit next," he said.

Cozzolino said seeing the community gather at the memorial was meaningful. "The way they do this, they have the steel flowers, flags. Very patriotic here," Cozzolino said. "This town's very diverse town, and it's a great town to live in." Cozzolino, a member of the Nam Knights Motorcycle Club of America, said the anniversary remains especially emotional for many first responders and veterans. "We have 84 chapters in the United States. We have 16 here, 17 here alone in Florida. About 1,400 members," Cozzolino said. "A lot of them were from New York. So, a lot of first responders, and a lot of them have the cancer now." The Port St. Lucie ceremony was one of several events across the region marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks.

hero.headline: Indian River County school bus driver arrested on child abuse charge
hero.teaser: A Sebastian woman who worked as a school bus driver for Indian River County schools was arrested after surveillance video allegedly showed her grabbing a student and bending the child's finger during an August incident.
hero.body:
A school bus driver in Indian River County was arrested Thursday on a child abuse charge following an investigation into an incident involving a student on a school bus, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Tracy Marie Alpy, 65, of Sebastian, was charged with one count of child abuse and was being held without bond, according to jail records.

Investigators reviewed school bus surveillance video related to an incident that happened Aug. 24 while Alpy was working as a bus driver for the School District of Indian River County, according to an arrest affidavit. The footage showed an interaction between Alpy and a student that led to the criminal investigation, deputies said.

The video appeared to show Alpy removing the child from a seat, grabbing the student and bending the child's finger, investigators wrote in the affidavit. Alpy could also be heard making a threatening remark toward the student during the encounter, deputies said. The child later told investigators they were frightened by what happened, according to the report. Deputies said they determined there was probable cause to arrest Alpy on the child abuse charge. Alpy declined to speak with investigators without an attorney present, the affidavit states.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after detectives find eight explosive devices at Balsam Drive home
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man after detectives serving a risk protection order Thursday discovered eight suspected explosive devices and bomb-making materials at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive.

Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

At approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday, detectives with the sheriff's office Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence when they identified suspected destructive devices. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team.

Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination of the suspected devices and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel. Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of the risk protection order.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us. Del Toro said the Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and bomb disposal technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove the devices. He thanked the FBI and ATF for their expertise and partnership as the investigation continues.

Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no immediate threat to the community.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police clear HCA Lawnwood Hospital after bomb threat; no devices found
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police cleared HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital on Saturday afternoon after investigating a bomb threat that prompted a temporary evacuation of visitors.

The Fort Pierce Police Department said just after 2 p.m. on September 12 that it was investigating a bomb threat at the hospital. Officers arrived and conducted an extensive search of the buildings. The department announced at 3:36 p.m. that no suspicious items or devices were found.

A hospital spokesperson confirmed there was a temporary evacuation of visitors and that patient care was never impacted.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 with remembrance ceremony
cards.teaser: Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered Friday morning at the Memorial Fountain at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center to honor victims and survivors of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, 25 years after the tragedy.
cards.body:
Community members, city leaders and first responders gathered Friday morning in Port St. Lucie to honor the victims and survivors of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, 25 years after the tragedy. The city's annual 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony was held at the Memorial Fountain at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center.

Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin, Police Chief Leo Niemczyk, St. Lucie County Fire District Firefighter/Paramedic Allen Civita and other local public safety leaders took part in the ceremony. Retired New York City Police Department detective Rafael Diaz served as the guest speaker, and the Port St. Lucie High School Choir performed.

Port St. Lucie resident Michael Cozzolino said the anniversary brought back memories of watching the attacks unfold while he was in Florida for work. Cozzolino was living in Connecticut at the time and had to drive back in a rental car with others. He said the uncertainty in the hours after the attacks was frightening, especially as a defense contractor who did not know where the next attack would occur.

Cozzolino, a member of the Nam Knights Motorcycle Club of America, said the anniversary remains especially emotional for many first responders and veterans. The club has 84 chapters in the United States and 16 or 17 chapters in Florida alone, with about 1,400 members. Many members were from New York, and many first responders now have cancer, he said. The Port St. Lucie ceremony was one of several events across the region marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks.

hero.headline: Martin County breaks world record with 400-foot Cuban sandwich in Palm City
hero.body:
Martin County now holds the world record for longest Cuban sandwich after Old Havana Cafe and House of Hope built a 400-foot sandwich Saturday morning in Palm City. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi completed the final measurement confirming the sandwich reached 400 feet. The massive sandwich broke the previous world record held by Tampa.

The event raised more than $30,000 for House of Hope, a Martin County nonprofit that provides food assistance, job training, education and other services aimed at helping local families become more self-sufficient.

A large crowd turned out to watch volunteers and sandwich builders assemble the record-breaking Cuban sandwich and support the fundraiser. Organizers said the event was designed to bring the community together while raising awareness and support for House of Hope's mission.

hero.headline: Palm City builds 400-foot Cuban sandwich, breaks Tampa world record
hero.body:
Martin County now claims to have built the world's longest Cuban sandwich. Community members produced a 400-foot-long sandwich at LCpl. Justin Wilson Memorial Park on Sandpiper Way in Palm City. The previous record was 365 feet, set in Tampa in 2024.

The event, called "Bite Into History: The Longest Cuban Sandwich Ever Made," was a joint effort of Old Havana Cafe at 2225 SE Ocean Blvd. and the nonprofit House of Hope, which serves Martin County. Organizers said it was to call attention to issues of food insecurity in the area, foster community spirit and celebrate Hispanic heritage. Members of the public could purchase sandwiches.

The event's presenting sponsor, the Doris M. Carter Family Foundation, pledged to double every donor's impact in the community by matching every donation made through the event up to $15,000.

Founded in 1984, House of Hope is a nonprofit organization that empowers Martin County residents to overcome hunger and hardship. House of Hope touches the lives of more than 30,000 people each month, helping with basic needs such as food, clothing, furniture, financial assistance, as well as longer-term case management services. The organization has service centers in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Jensen Beach, with thrift stores in Stuart, Hobe Sound and Indiantown. House of Hope also operates the Growing Hope Farm in Palm City and several nutrition gardens that provide sustainable sources of fresh produce for clients as well as nutrition education and vocational opportunities to the community.

A Cuban sandwich, or a cubano, is ham, roasted pork, Swiss cheese, pickles, mustard and sometimes salami on Cuban bread. There is rivalry between Tampa and Miami on who has the best sandwich. In 2012, the Tampa City Council named it the city's official "signature sandwich."

cards.headline: Martin County High School bomb threat traced to Russia, sheriff's office says
cards.body:
A bomb threat at Martin County High School prompted the evacuation of students and staff Thursday afternoon, with investigators now suspecting the threat originated from Russia, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The threat was sent via email Thursday afternoon, leading to an immediate response from law enforcement. The Martin County School District notified families that there was an increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to the emailed bomb threat. All students and staff were evacuated away from campus buildings while authorities conducted their investigation.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted a comprehensive search of the property Thursday afternoon. After completing the search, law enforcement determined that no threat actually existed. The district confirmed later Thursday that no evidence of a threat was found.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed on Friday that they are investigating the incident and suspect the threat originated out of Russia. The sheriff's office continues to investigate the hoax threat.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after 8 explosive devices found at home on Balsam Drive
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man is in custody after St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives discovered eight suspected explosive devices at his home while serving a risk protection order Thursday.

Detectives identified suspected destructive devices at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive around 12:20 p.m. Thursday, prompting a street closure that lasted roughly 10 to 14 hours as investigators removed the explosives. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives — possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices.

Morrone allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the risk protection order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team responded and safely removed seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades that had been modified. Morrone admitted to tampering with them, according to his arrest report.

After obtaining a search warrant, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, bringing the total to eight. The sheriff's office said investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were taken from the home related to the risk protection order. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the investigation underscores the seriousness of what detectives encountered. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices," Del Toro said.

According to court records, a judge granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others. The document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. The order required Morrone to surrender his firearms and ammunition immediately.

Morrone's son told WPTV he does not believe his father was planning to use the devices to harm anyone. The investigation remains ongoing.

hero.teaser: Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, faces eight counts after St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives serving a risk protection order Thursday found eight improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials at his residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man Friday on eight counts of explosives, possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after detectives serving a risk protection order discovered improvised explosive devices at his home. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, was arrested and charged following the investigation that began Thursday at his residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Detectives with the SLCSO Targeted Violence Unit were serving a risk protection order at the residence at approximately 12:20 p.m. Thursday when they identified suspected destructive devices, Fort Pierce police said in a news release Friday morning. Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination of the suspected devices and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel.

Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. This brought the total number of improvised explosive devices recovered from the residence to eight. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of a risk protection order.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," Sheriff Richard Del Toro said. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices. I'm proud of their professionalism and courage, and grateful for the expertise and partnership of the FBI and ATF as we continue this investigation." The investigation remains ongoing, and there is no immediate threat to the community.

Neighbors expressed concern about the situation. "That's really bad," Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, told WPBF. Rates described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. "It's a really nice neighborhood. That's the first I've ever heard of anything happening around here," he said.

cards.headline: Martin County bomb threat believed to have originated from Russia, sheriff says
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed Friday that investigators suspect the bomb threat that emptied Martin County High School originated from Russia.

Law enforcement evacuated students and staff from the campus Thursday afternoon after receiving the emailed threat. The sheriff's office conducted a comprehensive search of the property and determined no actual threat existed.

The Martin County School District notified families Thursday in an email that all students and staff had been evacuated away from campus buildings while law enforcement searched the property. The district reported an increased law enforcement presence on campus in response to the threat.

The district confirmed later Thursday that no evidence of a threat was found. The sheriff's office investigation into the origin of the threat continues.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested after 8 explosive devices found at home on Balsam Drive
hero.body:
A Fort Pierce man is in custody after investigators found eight improvised explosive devices at his home while serving a risk protection order.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office began its investigation Thursday around 12:20 p.m. when detectives identified suspected destructive devices at a residence in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, allowed deputies to search his home and car to retrieve weapons and ammunition in accordance with the order. During that search, detectives saw what appeared to be military-style hand grenades inside the house.

Deputies say seven devices appearing to be replica hand grenades were modified, and Morrone admitted to tampering with them. The sheriff's office Bomb Disposal Team safely removed the seven devices from the residence. After obtaining a search warrant, investigators found an additional improvised explosive device, bringing the total to eight. Investigators also located a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Investigators have not said whether any of the devices are functional.

Neighbors said the street was closed for roughly 10 to 14 hours Thursday as investigators removed the explosives from the home. Morrone's son, who was loading a truck with ammunition from inside the home, said he does not believe his father was planning to use the devices to harm anyone.

Morrone was arrested and charged with eight counts of explosives — possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices. Eight firearms were also taken from the home related to the risk protection order. He is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

According to court records, a judge granted the risk protection order after finding reasonable cause to believe Morrone posed a significant danger to himself or others. The document states Morrone had recently been involved in an act or threat of violence and had recently used or threatened to use a weapon. The order required Morrone to surrender his firearms and ammunition immediately.

"This investigation underscores the seriousness of what our detectives encountered and the importance of being alert to the threats around us," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. "Our Targeted Violence Unit detectives recognized the potential danger and took immediate action, and our Bomb Disposal Team technicians put themselves in harm's way to safely secure and remove these devices."

hero.headline: Martin County leaders call for return to post-9/11 unity at Palm City bridge walk
hero.teaser: County leaders and residents crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge in Palm City on Friday carrying photographs of attack victims as speakers urged a return to the cooperation felt immediately after Sept. 11, 2001.
hero.body:
Martin County leaders and residents marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks Friday morning with a memorial bridge walk in Palm City, where speakers called for a return to the unity Americans experienced in the days after the attacks.

The annual event at Jock Leighton Park near Veterans Memorial Bridge honored the nearly 3,000 people killed during the terrorist attacks. Participants crossed Veterans Memorial Bridge carrying photographs representing nearly every person who died during the attacks on the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and aboard hijacked airplanes.

Martin County Commission Chair Sarah Heard said the country responded with "unity, civility, respect, cooperation, generosity" following the attacks. "We were the United States. This is what I choose to remember," Heard said. Several leaders throughout the ceremony referenced Sept. 12, 2001, describing it as a moment when Americans came together despite political and personal differences. Commissioner Stacey Hetherington also reflected on the sense of togetherness Americans experienced after the attacks. "September 12th is also remembered because we united, we came together and we worked in unity," Hetherington said.

Community volunteer Mayce DelValle, who helped organize the memorial walk, said many people at Friday's ceremony expressed a longing to see that spirit return. "September 12th was a big day," DelValle said. "That was the day that the world actually came together in unity — neighbors hugging neighbors, friends helping friends, strangers embracing strangers. That's what we need to focus on. That is how we can truly honor those that perished." DelValle also carried photographs honoring Mark Zepplin and Kevin Marlowe, people she personally knew who died in the Twin Towers. "These guys were like family to me," DelValle said. "They unfortunately lost their lives in the buildings at the Twin Towers at Ground Zero on that day."

Martin County Fire Rescue Chief Chad Cianciulli described the patriotism that emerged immediately following the attacks. Chaplain Hoss Wiggins led a prayer before participants began the memorial walk, saying "After that awful event, the next day, a nation united in prayer."

Chaplain Hoss Wiggins continued the theme during a prayer delivered before participants began the memorial walk. “After that awful event, the next day, a nation united in prayer,” Wiggins said. “They set aside their differences and they united, and they cried out to God Almighty for help.” Wiggins said memorial events taking place across the country serve as reminders not to forget the sacrifices made by victims, first responders and military members. “The word of God encourages us over and over and over again to remember or don’t forget,” Wiggins said. “And that’s what we’re here today to do is to remember those who paid the ultimate sacrifice.” Before leading the crowd in prayer, Wiggins energized participants with a phrase familiar to many firefighters gathered at the event. “What I mean by ‘let the big dog eat,’ you simply focus on the task at hand,” Wiggins said before encouraging the crowd to respond together. Wiggins then prayed for the protection of first responders, local communities and the nation. As communities nationwide mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, local ceremonies like the Palm City memorial walk continue to focus not only on remembrance, but also on restoring the unity and shared purpose many Americans say they experienced in the days following the attacks. Every American chose unity, civility, respect, cooperation, generosity. New York City was unrecognizable, buried in widespread rubble. cards.headline: Bomb threat email forced evacuation at Martin County High School; FBI involved
cards.body:
A bomb threat email sent Thursday afternoon forced the evacuation of Martin County High School and triggered a multi-agency investigation now involving the FBI. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the email threatened three bombs on campus and claimed they would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m.

Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. Budensiek said the person living at that address appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia. The sheriff said the incident may be linked to a broader pattern of swatting cases.

"The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said. He added that the person named in the email is from Ukraine.

Deputies went to the Stuart residence, and Budensiek said the person has been cooperative. Investigators are conducting forensics to confirm the account was hacked and the email originated from Russia. The Martin County Sheriff's Office contacted the FBI tip line as part of the investigation.

The school was evacuated and parents were notified. Deputies swept the campus and found no credible threat. The school day resumed after the all-clear. Budensiek said public safety is his top priority.

I planted three bombs (gave the location) and don't waste your time looking for them because they're going to go off by 3 o'clock or 2:30 p.m.,'" Budensiek said. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said. hero.headline: Martin County High School evacuated after bomb threat email traced to hacked Stuart account
hero.body:
Martin County High School was evacuated Thursday afternoon after an email threatened a bomb attack at the campus. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, school district, and FBI tip line responded to the threat. Deputies conducted a sweep and determined there was no credible threat. The school day resumed after the all-clear.

Sheriff John Budensiek said the email claimed the sender planted three bombs at the school and warned they would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. The Stuart resident appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia, according to Budensiek.

Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. Deputies were at the Stuart home, and the resident cooperated with investigators. The sheriff said investigators must verify through forensics that the email was hacked and came from Russia. Budensiek said the person named in the email is from Ukraine.

Parents were notified during the evacuation. Budensiek emphasized that public safety is his top priority. The investigation continues as authorities work to confirm the details of the hacked account and explore possible connections to a broader pattern of swatting incidents.
hero.article_text: An email threatening a bomb attack at Martin County High School on Thursday afternoon led to an evacuation and a law enforcement response involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the school district, and the FBI's tip line. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the email raised concerns. "And the email says, 'I'm this male (not going to name him). I hate this school (Martin County High School). I planted three bombs (gave the location) and don't waste your time looking for them because they're going to go off by 3 o'clock or 2:30 p.m.,'" Budensiek said. Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. "We are at the individual's home; they've been cooperative so far. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said. The school was evacuated, parents were notified, and deputies conducted a sweep of the campus. After determining there was no credible threat, the school day resumed. Loring said the journey was long and arduous, but the city feels the park will generate new interest in the community and be a sincere benefit to residents.

Loring said the city has significant room for growth and has been hidden from view for many years. He said people are just now noticing Fellsmere's lands and surrounding amenities. He said the city has significant potential.

hero.headline: Two arrested in Indian River County for illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over Labor Day weekend
hero.body:
Indian River County deputies arrested two men in separate cases involving alleged illegal saw palmetto berry harvesting over the Labor Day weekend, according to arrest affidavits.

Corey Michael Smith of Vero Beach was arrested Sept. 4 after deputies responded to a trespassing call at a BP gas station on 9th Street Southwest. A helicopter crew had spotted Smith on Indian River County School Board property near 800 20th Avenue. Deputies found him at the gas station with five black bags containing saw palmetto stalks.

Smith showed deputies a palmetto berry harvesting permit that listed an address on 17th Avenue Southwest. The property owner told deputies Smith did not have permission to harvest on the property, which belongs to the Salvation Army. Smith was arrested on charges of using a false or forged palmetto berry harvest permit, disclosing police radio information to aid a suspect, and trespassing after a warning. A deputy heard dispatch traffic coming from a scanner app on Smith's phone while he was detained, the affidavit states.

Francis Ostrowski was arrested a day later after a sheriff's office camera in the North County Conservation Area near 7800 130th Street captured a man carrying a bag filled with saw palmetto berries. Deputies located Ostrowski nearby with a bag of berries and asked whether he had a permit to harvest them. Ostrowski said he did not. He was arrested on a felony charge of harvesting an endangered plant without a permit.

The arrests come amid a series of recent saw palmetto berry cases across the Treasure Coast. CBS12 previously reported on arrests involving the alleged theft of about 200 pounds of berries in Martin County and about 150 pounds in Indian River County. In another recent case, a Boynton Beach man was arrested after deputies said they found about 500 pounds of saw palmetto berries.

Keith Anthony Morrone, 57, of Fort Pierce, was arrested Friday and charged with eight counts of possessing, making or attempting to make destructive devices after the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Disposal Team recovered improvised explosive devices and bomb-making materials from his home in the 6000 block of Balsam Drive. Morrone is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a $20,000 bond.

Detectives secured the residence and surrounding area and requested assistance from the Bomb Disposal Team. Bomb technicians conducted a preliminary examination and removed seven devices from the residence, safely securing them in a containment vessel.

Detectives subsequently obtained a search warrant for the residence. During the execution of the search warrant, investigators located an additional improvised explosive device, which was safely secured and removed. This brought the total number of improvised explosive devices recovered from the residence to eight. Investigators also found a large quantity of materials used in the construction of explosive devices. Eight firearms were also taken into custody pursuant to the service of the risk protection order.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce honors 9/11 victims at Veterans Memorial Park ceremony
cards.teaser: The Treasure Coast community gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed and those impacted by the attacks. The ceremony included a wreath-laying for Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93.
cards.body:
The Treasure Coast community gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, first responders, veterans, and others impacted by the attacks.

The ceremony included a wreath-laying to honor Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93, which crashed into a Pennsylvania field after passengers and crew fought back against the hijackers. Her final phone call to her husband deeply moved the crowd. "I hope to be able to see your face again, baby. I love you, bye," Lyles said in her last call.

Jerome Sangalli, a United Airlines International Purser AFA-CWA Boston and former union vice-president, described the emotional impact of hearing her words. "I held it together until I heard that phone call. I was just rushed back to when 9/11 happened," Sangalli said. He also expressed his admiration for the bravery of those aboard Flight 93. "All the flight attendants, all the pilots, they're all angels," Sangalli said.

Dennis McWilliams, who lost four family members on 9/11, shared how his family has used their tragic memories to strengthen their bond. "Our family has taken a stance to use those awful tragic memories at our family reunions, at our weddings, at our funerals to bring ourselves closer to one another," McWilliams said.

The ceremony also carried a message of unity, with local officials calling for the nation to recapture the sense of togetherness felt after the attacks. "I think we should use the memories of 9/11 to unite our country again, to remember those feelings of pride that we had in the immediate aftermath of such a tragic loss," McWilliams said.

"At the end of the day, we need to come back together as we did on that fateful day and months and years after. The United States has to come back together," Fort Pierce Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky said.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff links bomb threat at high school to Russia-based swatting scheme
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek confirmed Thursday that a bomb threat email which forced the evacuation of Martin County High School is linked to a broader swatting trend, with investigators tracing the hacked email account to Russia and a Ukrainian victim in Stuart.

The threatening email arrived Thursday afternoon, prompting an immediate evacuation and response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the school district, and the FBI's tip line. The email claimed the sender had planted three bombs at Martin County High School that would detonate by 2:30 p.m. or 3 p.m.

Investigators traced the email address to a home in Stuart. The individual at that Stuart residence appears to be a victim whose account was hacked from Russia before the threatening email was sent. Budensiek said the person who lives at that Stuart address is from Ukraine and has been cooperative with investigators.

"The individual that we're dealing with in the city of Stuart appears at that time to be victimized himself. His account looks like it was hacked from Russia, and then this email from Russia, so this is a trend we've seen over and over again," Budensiek said.

Budensiek said the incident may be linked to other swatting cases. Investigators are conducting forensic analysis to confirm the email was hacked and originated from Russia.

Parents were notified of the threat and the school was evacuated. Deputies conducted a sweep of the campus. After determining there was no credible threat, the school day resumed.

"We are at the individual's home; they've been cooperative so far. But we've got to check the boxes, go through the forensics side of it, and make sure that that email was indeed hacked. It did indeed come from Russia; we can see that part at this point, but we've got some things to vet out. Our person in that email is ironically from Ukraine," Budensiek said.

The sheriff emphasized that public safety is his top priority.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport opens $3M renovation with dual baggage claim, covered walkways
hero.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport has completed a $3 million renovation project that is now open to passengers, featuring dual baggage claim gates, covered walkways, and a new courtyard seating area. Airport officials said the upgrades were designed to improve the travel experience for passengers.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said the new terminal includes two baggage claim gates located about 100 feet from where aircraft park. The project also added canopies over passenger walkways and baggage claim areas, along with a courtyard where passengers can wait for their flights.

Passenger Austin Garafola said the improvements represent a substantial upgrade from previous conditions. "Oh, it's definitely a lot better than it was. You go right in right under the awning, and then everything is so much better. We used to have to wait in single file coming out; you get rained on, you get everything, but yeah, significantly better," Garafola said. Passenger Doris Newell called the facility great and praised the accessibility.

Airport officials announced plans for a concession area for departing passengers, and new long-term parking has been approved. The airport serves three commercial airlines: American, JetBlue and Breeze. Dambeck said the upgrades will create a better experience for passengers as they wait for their flights. Officials also plan to seek public input later this year on discussion about a possible new terminal.

Lucie County Sheriff’s Office. Neighbors expressed concern about the situation. “That’s really bad,” Terry Rates, who has lived in the neighborhood for 10 years, told WPBF's Ari Hait. Rates described the area as peaceful and said he was surprised to see such activity near his home. “It’s a really nice neighborhood. That’s the first I’ve ever heard of anything happening around here,” he said. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce native CeeCee Lyles honored at Flight 93 Memorial on 25th anniversary of 9/11
cards.teaser: The family of CeeCee Ross Lyles, a Fort Pierce flight attendant who died on United Flight 93, gathered in Shanksville, Pennsylvania this week for the 25th anniversary ceremony at the Flight 93 Memorial.
cards.body:
The family of CeeCee Ross Lyles, a Fort Pierce flight attendant who died on United Flight 93, gathered in Shanksville, Pennsylvania this week for the 25th anniversary ceremony at the Flight 93 Memorial. Lyles and other passengers and crew fought back against hijackers on Sept. 11, 2001, forcing the plane to crash into a field in Pennsylvania and preventing it from reaching its intended target in Washington, D.C.

A statue stands in Lyles' honor on the shores of the Indian River Lagoon in Fort Pierce. Her husband said at the anniversary, "The 25th anniversary. I feel like every day or, well, almost every day, because her picture is all around the house. You know, I really miss her. She was such a beautiful woman."

Lyles grew up in Fort Pierce and served as a police officer and detective before pursuing her childhood dream of becoming a flight attendant. She had been in the role for just 10 months before Sept. 11. That day, 19 minutes into the hijacking, Lyles called her husband and left a message on their answering machine. "Baby, you have to listen to me carefully," she said. Calmly, she asked him to tell her sons, Jerome and Javon, that she loved them. Moments later, passengers and crew stormed the cockpit.

Today, Lyles' sons are parents themselves. "She would have three grandkids. She would have three for myself and three from Javon. So she would be arms full at the moment. Yes, she would," said Jerome. "Twenty-five years is … it's been a long time of missing her and, you know, wishing she was here with her family and kids and my kids and, you know, a lot of, a lot of moments, like a lot of, you know, cherished moments have been missed," he added.

Lyles' brother, Tony, said, "She was a good, good, good sister that cared about people. And I just miss her with all my heart and just glad to have been a part of her life for as long as I was." A family member said, "One good thing that came out of it was that the nation and all and everybody just came together in a spirit of unity, and that seemed to have lasted for a couple of months. And I pray that as we enter into this 25th year anniversary, that we can celebrate that spirit of unity."

Each year, the family awards scholarships in Lyles' name to graduating seniors, who must write an essay about her life to earn it. Some family members say the community they have found at the Shanksville memorial now feels like family of its own.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce ceremony honors 9/11 victims, hometown hero CeeCee Lyles
cards.teaser: Community members gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce to remember the nearly 3,000 people killed in the September 11 attacks and pay special tribute to Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93.
cards.body:
Community members gathered at Veterans Memorial Park in Fort Pierce for a 9/11 remembrance ceremony honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, first responders, veterans, and others impacted by the attacks.

The ceremony included a wreath-laying to honor Fort Pierce native CeeCee Ross Lyles, a flight attendant aboard United Airlines Flight 93, which crashed into a Pennsylvania field after passengers and crew fought back against the hijackers. Her final phone call to her husband moved the crowd.

"I hope to be able to see your face again, baby. I love you, bye," Lyles said in her last call.

Jerome Sangalli, a United Airlines International Purser AFA-CWA Boston and former union vice-president, described the emotional impact of hearing her words. "I held it together until I heard that phone call. I was just rushed back to when 9/11 happened," Sangalli said. "All the flight attendants, all the pilots, they're all angels."

Dennis McWilliams, who lost four family members on 9/11, shared how his family has used their tragic memories to strengthen their bond. "Our family has taken a stance to use those awful tragic memories at our family reunions, at our weddings, at our funerals to bring ourselves closer to one another," McWilliams said.

The ceremony carried a message of unity, encouraging attendees to remember the sense of togetherness felt after the attacks. "I think we should use the memories of 9/11 to unite our country again, to remember those feelings of pride that we had in the immediate aftermath of such a tragic loss," McWilliams said.

Fort Pierce Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky echoed the call for unity. "At the end of the day, we need to come back together as we did on that fateful day and months and years after. The United States has to come back together," Dzadovsky said.

hero.headline: Maryland man arrested in Martin County on child sex charges after Roblox chat with 12-year-old bonds out
hero.teaser: A 22-year-old Maryland man arrested in Martin County on charges related to an inappropriate online relationship with a 12-year-old girl has bonded out of jail. Investigators are probing possible additional victims.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old Maryland man arrested in Martin County on charges related to an inappropriate online relationship with a 12-year-old girl has bonded out of jail after posting a $30,000 bond. Ting Bawi was booked into the Martin County Jail on Wednesday following an investigation that began with a tip alleging he was sending inappropriate messages and requesting explicit photos from a teenager.

Bawi met the victim through the online game Roblox, where she had claimed to be 16, according to the arrest report. The victim told investigators during an interview in Martin County that she and Bawi began communicating in 2025. Text messages included in the report show Bawi writing, "You belong to me," "I can't wait to have you in my possession," and expressing a desire to "make a kid" with her. Officials said their conversations made it clear she was in middle school.

Officials said they discovered child sexual abuse material on Bawi's phone. Investigators are probing the possibility of additional victims.

Investigators in Baltimore County did not charge Bawi with sexual solicitation of a minor, as Maryland's age of consent is 16, which the victim had listed on her Roblox account. Bawi faces charges in Martin County related to the inappropriate online relationship with the minor.

Officials said they discovered child sexual abuse material on his phone and are investigating the possibility of additional victims. The arrest report states that Bawi met the victim, a 12-year-old girl, through the online game Roblox, where she had claimed to be 16. However, officials said their conversations made it clear she was in middle school. The victim, who was interviewed in Martin County, told investigators that she and Bawi began communicating in 2025. Text messages included in the report show Bawi writing, "You belong to me," "I can't wait to have you in my possession," and expressing a desire to "make a kid" with her. Despite his arrest in Florida, investigators in Baltimore County did not charge Bawi with sexual solicitation of a minor, as Maryland's age of consent is 16, which the victim had listed on her Roblox account. Bawi was booked into the Martin County Jail on Wednesday on a warrant for his arrest. He was held on a $30,000 bond and has since bonded out. cards.headline: Martin County High School reopens after bomb threat evacuation; investigation continues
cards.body:
Martin County High School students and staff returned to class Thursday afternoon after a bomb threat email prompted an evacuation and campus-wide search. The Martin County Sheriff's Office completed a sweep of the school and found no evidence of a threat, clearing the campus to resume normal operations.

School officials notified families of the bomb threat Thursday afternoon and ordered an evacuation as law enforcement responded. Students and staff remained away from campus buildings while authorities conducted a comprehensive search of the school property.

At 2:55 p.m., school administrators sent an update confirming the Sheriff's Office had finalized its sweep and found nothing suspicious. Students and staff returned to their classrooms, and regular dismissal proceeded as scheduled. Bus transportation operated without delays.

"Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we worked with law enforcement to ensure the safety of our students and staff," school officials said in the message to families. Authorities have not released additional details about the source of the email threat. The investigation continues.

School administrators emphasized throughout the incident that all students and staff remained safe. "Please know that students and staff remain safe," the school said in its initial notification to families. "We will provide an update once there is new information to share."

The evacuation marked a disruption to the school day as law enforcement worked to verify whether the emailed threat posed any actual danger. The Sheriff's Office maintained an increased presence on campus during the response.
